claims.explanation: CGS-15943 is a nonselective adenosine receptor antagonist, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by adenosine-receptor-dependent cAMP/PKA signaling and oxidative-stress/NFE2L2-linked survival programs rather than by a single lineage. Lines with EGFR/MAPK-pathway activation, PTEN loss, or NFE2L2/KEAP1 alterations appear enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with dependence on adenosine/cAMP and redox homeostasis, while BRAF-mutant melanoma and several TP53-only lines are relatively protected.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the most killed
PTEN loss in ZR751 and other sensitive lines may increase PI3K/AKT dependence
NFE2L2-mutant colorectal lines SNUC5 and HEC265 are among the least affected
KEAP1-mutant HEC265 is among the least affected, suggesting redox adaptation
BRAF-mutant melanomas UACC62 and IPC298 are relatively resistant
KRAS-mutant colorectal lines CL11 and SNU410 are among the least affected
CGS-15943 targets ADORA2A; high receptor expression may increase dependence on adenosine signaling
CGS-15943 also antagonizes ADORA1, which can modulate cAMP and survival
ADORA2B is expressed in myeloid/neutrophil-like contexts and is a CGS-15943 target
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is weak but appears in many protected lines
CDKN2A-mutant lines SNU1214, MHHES1, and IPC298 are among the least affected
SMARCA4-mutant KYSE270 is among the most killed, though evidence is limited
